fire: Young men sailed for Alaska, sure they would find gold and come home wealthy.
The old posters sold the glamour of steamship voyages to faraway islands.
In the spice market of Marrakesh, lanterns glowed over piles of saffron.
Treasure hunters still dream of the sunken galleons off the Florida coast.
The novel captures the mystique of caravans crossing the desert by moonlight.
Adventurers flocked to the frontier hoping to make their fortunes overnight.
At the masked ball in Venice, strangers danced in velvet and silk.
Explorers wrote of jungle temples and the lure of lost cities.
quiet: Young men drove to the office, sure they would finish the report by noon.
The old posters listed the bus times for the route to the airport.
In the grocery store downtown, the lights buzzed over the frozen peas.
Accountants still argue about the new tax forms for small businesses.
The manual explains how to replace the filter in the kitchen tap.
Commuters crowded the platform hoping the train would arrive on time.
At the school meeting, parents discussed the new lunch schedule.
Inspectors wrote of cracked pipes and the cost of a new boiler.
